blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The basic average is calculated by dividing the sum of all observations by the total count of observations.
The total sum of a series can be easily found by multiplying the average by the number of observations.
Adding or removing a value from a group shifts the total sum and modifies the group average.
In age-related problems, time changes (past/future) must be applied equally to every individual in the group.
Weighted averages are used when combining multiple groups that have different sizes or weights.
Average of a group of numbers is a single value that represents the central value of the group.

Formula:

Average = (Sum of observations) / (Number of observations)

blocks.content: In SSC examination, questions on average are direct, formula-based, and often linked with age, salary, marks, population and similar topics.

blocks.content: 3. FINDING SUM WHEN AVERAGE IS GIVEN

items:
Formula:

Sum = Average × Number of observations

Example:

Average age of 10 students is 18 years.

Total age = 18 × 10 = 180 years

blocks.content: 4. AVERAGE WHEN A VALUE IS ADDED OR REMOVED

Example 1:

Average of 5 numbers is 20. A new number 30 is added.

Old sum = 20 × 5 = 100

New sum = 100 + 30 = 130

New number of observations = 6

New average = 130 / 6 ≈ 21.67



Example 2:

Average of 10 numbers is 25. One number 35 is removed.

Old sum = 25 × 10 = 250

New sum = 250 − 35 = 215

New number of observations = 9

New average = 215 / 9 ≈ 23.89

items: Average age of 5 boys is 20 years and average age of 3 girls is 18 years.
Sum of boys = 5 × 20 = 100
Sum of girls = 3 × 18 = 54
Total sum = 154

Total persons = 8



Average age = 154 / 8 = 19.25 years

rows: Varying weights assigned to different items
Combining groups with unequal sizes or importance

blocks.content:
Weighted average is used when groups have different sizes.

Example:

items: Average marks of 20 students is 60 and average marks of 30 students is 50.

Total students = 50



Average marks = 2700 / 50 = 54

blocks.content:
• Always calculate total sum first.

• Be careful when values are added or removed.

• Average depends on sum and number of terms.

• SSC questions are generally simple and direct.

items: Questions involving finding the weight or age of a newly added or replaced member are heavily tested.
In age questions, remember that if n years pass, the average age of a group of people also increases by n years.
Be careful to divide by the sum of weights, not the count of items, when calculating weighted averages.
